name: Bentley Commons
award: 2022 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Bentley Commons is a 192-home affordable community in southeast Colorado Springs: three local nonprofits renovated the 24 existing apartments and built 168 new ones for households at 30% to 60% of AMI, including units for formerly homeless veterans with VASH vouchers. It won $2,735,647 a year in federal 4% credit and $1,000,000 in state credit in CHFA's 2022 Round Two.
why_it_matters: It shows a locally owned nonprofit joint venture taking a site rescued from a failed condo project in 2009 to full build-out, with the city's bond cap, a housing authority tax-exemption partnership, a county housing authority loan and project-based VASH vouchers, and no out-of-state developer.

status.label: Completed and open: grand opening 2025-10-07
status.detail: Financing closed in December 2023 and ground was broken on 2024-01-30. Partners in Housing said on 2025-10-03 that construction was complete on all 192 units, and the partners held a grand opening on 2025-10-07. No placed-in-service or 8609 record was found.

next_step: Watch for CHFA's property records or the sponsors' reports to show the placed-in-service year and stabilized occupancy.

background.text: In 2009 the three nonprofits used Neighborhood Stabilization Program funds to buy a bankrupt, abandoned 24-unit condominium property known as Bentley Commons, the only two buildings a private developer finished before the 2008 crash, and ran it as affordable rentals.
The partners later bought an adjacent parcel to build out the site; much of the expansion had been approved for the earlier condo developer before the recession.

Part of the site sits next to a historic inert landfill; buried material on the site was to be removed, buildings get sub-slab vapor barriers, and methane monitoring wells stay in use, under a plan approved in CDPHE's Voluntary Cleanup Program.

Rehab of the 24 existing units: the application planned new HVAC, accessibility updates, community and leasing space changes and new siding; by December 2024 the work also covered mold remediation, mechanical rooms, water heaters, furnaces, air conditioning, flooring and paint, and was complete.
The application planned a property tax exemption through a partnership with the Colorado Springs Housing Authority and 25 project-based VASH vouchers administered by the VA.
No asterisk footnote applies to this row in the award report; its asterisks only key the Type and Target codes.

discrepancies.text: The award report names the City of Colorado Springs as bond issuer for $30,000,000, but CHFA held the bond hearing for CHFA-issued bonds of up to $39,000,000, and the sponsors say the financing is through CHFA.
CHFA's award description and the application say 25 VASH units, while CHFA's 2023 bond notice and later reporting say 28 units for formerly homeless veterans.
The application said renovations would not require relocating tenants, but existing residents were temporarily moved for a couple of weeks to a month during the rehab.

The address appears as 2730 Bentley Point with ZIP 80901 in the award report, 2730 Bentley Point with ZIP 80910 in the application, 2710-2730 Bentley Point in the bond notice and 2715 Bentley Point in the sponsors' completion notice.
The total cost is reported as close to $65 million by KOAA and the Gazette and as $64 million in the Colorado Public Radio article.
